description: Procedural Skills Approval Panel -- review interface for auto-extracted fix patterns learned from successful workflow runs. When a workflow iterates 3+ times and produces an effective fix (reuse_count >= 2), the fix pattern is captured as a reusable skill with source='auto' and approval_status='pending'. Users review pending skills here and approve or reject them; approved skills are injected into future worker agent prompts during the agentic phase (up to 10 skills, 2000-char token budget). The self-repair loop auto-disables approved skills that cause 3+ consecutive verification failures by reverting them to 'pending'. Data source: GET /skills fetches from user_skills table (SQLite), filtered client-side to source='auto'. Approval mutations use POST /skills/{id}/approve. Skill metrics available at GET /graph/skill-metrics. Skills are also mirrored to PG observations (topic_key='skill:<slug>') for cross-session full-text search, and materialized as Skill nodes in the knowledge graph with DerivedFrom, UsedIn, and Supersedes edges.

groups.description: Clicking the chevron expands a detail panel below the skill row, indented to align with the skill name. The panel shows labeled fields: Description (full text), Tags (comma-separated), Phases (comma-separated), and Created (localized datetime). For auto-extracted skills, a Provenance section appears with a muted background showing Fix type (monospace), Source run (monospace, 10px), Fix ID (monospace, 10px), and Effectiveness (green text). Provenance data is parsed from the skill's description field which embeds 'task_run: {id}, fix: {id}' and 'Fix type: {type}' patterns.

groups.description: Pending skills show inline Approve (green) and Reject (red) buttons in the row. Approved/rejected skills show these buttons in the expanded detail panel instead, along with a 'Reset to Pending' button (amber). All three buttons call POST /skills/{id}/approve with the target status. The UI updates optimistically -- the skill immediately moves to the new filter tab. If the API returns a non-ok response, the update is not applied (no rollback of optimistic state since the API call happens before the state update).
groups.name: Approval and Rejection Actions

groups.description: When a skill's approval status is changed, the filter tab counts must update immediately and the skill must appear under the correct filter. The state is managed client-side via React useState -- no page reload occurs. The API mutation (POST /skills/{id}/approve) fires before the state update, so a failed API call prevents the UI from changing.
groups.name: State Consistency After Mutations
